blocks.text: Fundamental Rights are constitutional guarantees that protect individual liberty and equality. They place limits on public power and can be enforced through the courts, subject to the Constitution’s provisions.

rows: Equality before law and prohibition of discrimination.
Specified freedoms and protections of life and liberty.
Prohibits trafficking, forced labour, and certain forms of child labour.
Freedom of conscience and religious practice, subject to limits.
Protects cultural interests and minority educational institutions.
Allows people to approach the Supreme Court to enforce rights.

blocks.text: When revising a right, note who it protects, what it guarantees, and whether the Constitution permits reasonable restrictions.
